Data table

Things compared across columns on a real table: a caption, sortable headers, numeric columns, one action for each row, rows that expand, and a stacked layout on a phone.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • When the reader compares the same facts across several things: runs by duration and tokens, repositories by usage, branches by age.
  • With the default stacked layout when each row can be read by itself on a phone: below 768px a row becomes a block and each cell prints its column label beside its value.
  • With the scroll variant when the reader compares down a column even on a phone, or when the headers sort: the columns stay and the table scrolls sideways inside its wrapper.
  • With the sticky variant for a table long enough that the header would scroll out of sight.

When not to use it

  • For things the reader scans and opens, with one or two facts each. Use the list.
  • For the facts of one thing. Use the key-value list.
  • For layout. A table is for data with column headers.
  • For a sortable table in the stacked layout. The header row is not drawn below 768px, so its buttons would be out of reach: use the scroll variant, or offer the order in a select above the table.
  • For a row with two or more actions. Open the row's own view, or put the rest in its detail row.
  • For a table nested in a table's detail row. Put facts there as text or a key-value list.

Variants

stacked
The default, with no modifier class. Columns at 768px and wider. Below that each row is a block: its th is the block's title and each td prints the label in its data-label attribute beside its value. The header row is not drawn.
scroll ds-data-table--scroll
Columns at every width. Put the table inside a div with the class ds-data-table__scroll, which scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit. Cells do not wrap.
sticky ds-data-table--sticky
The header row stays at the top of whatever scrolls the table up and down, on the page surface. It has no effect inside ds-data-table__scroll unless the app gives that wrapper a height, and none in the stacked layout below 768px.

Accessibility

  • Use a table with a caption, ds-data-table__caption, that says what the rows are. Column headers are th scope="col" in a thead, and the cell that names each row is a th scope="row". Do not build a table from divs.
  • Give every td a data-label attribute holding the text of its column header. Below 768px the stylesheet prints it beside the value, and it is read out with the value. Leave it off the action cell, a detail cell and a state cell.
  • A cell holds one run of text or one element. In the stacked layout a second element would start a new line under the label.
  • A column of numbers carries ds-data-table__numeric on its th and on every td: right-aligned, in tabular figures, each number with its unit.
  • A sortable header is a button with the class ds-data-table__sort inside the th, holding the header's words. Set aria-sort="ascending" or aria-sort="descending" on the th of the one column the rows are ordered by, and leave it off the others. The stylesheet draws the direction from that attribute. The app reorders the rows and moves the attribute, and the caption or a role="status" line says the new order.
  • A row has at most one action: a small quiet button in a td with the class ds-data-table__action, the last cell of the row, under a th whose text is in a ds-visually-hidden span. When every row's button has the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the row. The cell pads the 32px button out to 44px, so its pointer target fits the row and a one-line row is no taller.
  • A row that expands has a button with the class ds-data-table__expand in its th, holding the words that name the row, with aria-expanded and with aria-controls pointing at the next row. That next row is a tr with the class ds-data-table__detail holding one td that spans every column. The app sets aria-expanded to true or false and nothing else: the stylesheet does not draw the detail row while the button says false. Do not use the hidden attribute on the detail row.
  • Mark the selected row with aria-selected="true" on its tr. It is drawn with a bar at its start as well as a shade.
  • With no rows, while loading and after a failure, keep the caption and the header and put one row in the tbody whose single td has the class ds-data-table__state and spans every column. Empty: a ds-data-table__message sentence saying why, and at most one small button. Loading: a spinner with role="status", and aria-busy="true" on the table. Error: a ds-data-table__message with role="alert" that says what to do, and a small Retry button. The stylesheet draws the failure's icon.
  • A status in a cell is written in words. One badge may hold it.
  • The wrapper of the scroll variant carries tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-labelledby pointing at the caption's id, so a keyboard can scroll it with the arrow keys. Give each such table on a view a different caption.
  • Tab moves through the header buttons, then each row's expand button and action, in order. Enter and Space activate them. There are no arrow-key bindings between cells.
